subject: physics
question_text: Define surface tension. Write its SI unit and dimensional formula.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 16 (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: surface tension is the force acting per unit length on an imaginary line drawn in the surface of a liquid, T = F/l; SI unit N m⁻¹, dimensional formula [MT⁻²], matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 10.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Draw an imaginary line on the surface
of a liquid. Surface tension is the
force acting per unit length on this
line, tangential to the surface and
at right angles to the line:
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say force per unit length on an imaginary line, tangential to the surface and at right angles to the line, and give T = F/l.
steps.why: The direction matters as much as the size: surface tension acts along the surface itself, not into or out of it, which is why it is described as tangential to the surface.
common_mistakes: Saying surface tension acts perpendicular to the surface. It acts tangentially, along the surface.
Leaving out that the force is measured per unit length of the line, not per unit area.

recall.must_convey: That surface tension is the force per unit length on an imaginary line in the liquid's surface, acting tangentially to the surface and at right angles to the line: T = F/l.
accept: force per unit length on an imaginary line
reject: SI unit is N per metre

steps.memory_tip: Surface tension: force along the surface, per unit length of an imaginary line, T = F/l.

steps.label: SI unit and dimensional formula
lines: The SI unit of surface tension is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give both the SI unit N m⁻¹ and the dimensional formula [MT⁻²].
steps.why: Force per unit length carries the dimensions of force, [MLT⁻²], divided by length, [L], which cancels one power of length and leaves [MT⁻²].
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as N m instead of N m⁻¹.
Giving only the SI unit and leaving out the dimensional formula, or the other way round.

recall.must_convey: That the SI unit of surface tension is newton per metre, N m⁻¹, and its dimensional formula is [MT⁻²].
accept: dimensional formula M T power minus two
reject: force per unit length on an imaginary line

steps.memory_tip: Force over length: N m⁻¹ for the unit, [MT⁻²] for the dimensions.

insider_note: The second mark needs both the SI unit and the dimensional formula; one without the other is an incomplete answer.
